scope: Which object IDs a store read may request from the object-job port, and how a request the server partly rejects is split. Measured on Git 2.50.1 in explorations/repository-cache/results/gitlinks.json.

change_set.listing: git diff --raw -z --no-abbrev --no-renames <left> <right>, run with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 and the store read configuration; both sides of every entry are considered and the all-zero object ID is ignored.
rules: Only blob modes are requested. A tree never appears without -t and is present in a blobless store anyway.

A 160000 entry is a gitlink: its object ID names a commit in another repository. It is reported as a submodule entry, never requested, and never reported missing, even though cat-file --batch-check calls it missing.
An unknown mode is a typed unsupported_entry, never requested.

request.split: Try the whole list; if the server rejects it with a per-object rejection, split it into the first ceil(n/2) object IDs and the rest and retry each part; a rejected single object ID is marked unavailable individually.
request.terminal_rule: A terminal failure fails the whole job without splitting: splitting a list the server refuses as a policy would issue 2n - 1 requests for nothing.
request.request_bound: With r rejected object IDs among n, the split issues at most 1 + 2 * r * ceil(log2 n) requests.

request_cases.why: The measured flow: 11 blobs, one gitlink commit ID at position 4, and one object ID the origin does not have, against a file:// origin over protocol v2.
Measured with protocol v0 and no uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant: the server refused every unadvertised object, including blobs it has.
